new_statements.rule_in_words: Glavda is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with lexical tone classes for all major word classes and a rich system of grammatical/verbal tone rules (polar tone rule); lexical tone has low functional load. The authors make no statement about word stress or accent placement anywhere in the chapter that could be located.
new_statements.exceptions: none regarding stress; tone: bisyllabic stems LH, imperative and certain tense/mode forms fix tone patterns, polar tone rule between R-stem and preceding extension/subject marker (pp. 665-669).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical/grammatical tone at word level; read only through Google Books snippet view (no page images available), so the absence of a stress remark rests on Google's in-volume search returning no 'stress'/'accent' hits inside pp. 641-675 rather than on a full reading.
new_statements.identity_note: Buba & Owens 2007 describe the Glavda of Ngoshe (Gwoza LGA, Borno State, Nigeria), i.e. Hamm's dialect II (Ngoshe/Boko); Glottolog lists no sub-dialect codes under glav1244. Rapp's 1960s materials pair Glavda with 'Yaghwatadaxa' (a Guduf-Gava/gudu1252-area lect), which should not be conflated with Glavda.
